patch_description: The current constructor fixes centers on a hex lattice and only grows radii. The leftover space near walls/corners is wasted because centers never move. I propose adding a deterministic relaxation phase: after greedy radius growth, each center is pushed slightly away from touching neighbors and toward the interior from walls (Lloyd-style repulsion), then radii are re-grown. We keep the best configuration seen across iterations. This lets edge circles slide into corners and staggered rows shift to fill gaps, typically raising the sum of radii well above a static lattice. The process is fully deterministic (fixed iteration count, fixed order), so the constructor remains explicit and reproducible.
